title: Esau Ran to Meet Him
reflectionText: Jacob came bowing himself seven times to the ground. Esau simply ran. And when the weeping was over, Jacob said it plainly: I have seen your face, as one sees the face of God, and you were pleased with me. What is it to bow yourself that low to the ground, and be caught up instead into an embrace?
editorialNotes: Text-First Story Factory 2.0 Batch A (journey backlog G2, approved 2026-07-22). Genesis 33, adult lane absent; kid_jacob_esau covers Genesis 33:1-11 in the separate kid lane (adult-parity fill). Pairs with 1572 (Genesis 27) as the approved Jacob-arc resolution. Boundary: chapter 33 only — no Genesis 32 wrestling or fear-prayer retold; Jacob's dividing and ordering of the family is narrated as observable action with no imported fear-motive, and the twenty-year chronology from earlier chapters is not referenced. SHORT only (WEB 461w / KJV 361w): the complete faithful retelling of the 20-verse source (~477 WEB source words) sits inside the SHORT band; a FULL would require inflation beyond the source's honest ceiling (ADR-030/031). El Elohe Israel is rendered with its meaning for the listening ear. Ends on the chapter's own closure (the altar at Shechem). CODEX-AUDIT CORRECTION 2026-07-23. (Finding 6) the WEB semantic rendering 'in peace' was removed from the KJV lane, which now follows its own extract's 'Shalem, a city of Shechem' [RESOLVED at first remediation, re-confirmed]. (Finding 5) both reflections dropped the unsupported clause 'made ready for something else' — the reflection question is now grounded only in the stated seven bows (v3) and the running embrace (v4), importing no Genesis 32 fear-expectation [RESOLVED at first remediation; reflections unchanged in this commit]. (Finding 2) SECOND REMEDIATION (this commit): the first re-author (run 21/88.2% -> 8/46.4%) was judged still verse-sequential and had introduced a chronology contradiction ('Esau did not wait for the seventh bow', contradicting Gen 33:3 where all seven bows precede v4). Re-authored again from a scene outline into three compressed movements — the approach, family arrangement, seven completed bows, and embrace (vv1-4); the introductions and the gift refused-then-accepted (vv5-11); the parting and the journey to Succoth and Shalem (vv12-20). The chronology defect is fixed: all seven bows are completed before Esau runs. Current metrics: run 8 / coverage 36.3% / 361w. WEB short and both reflections unchanged.
